headline: High: dexter’s broad network egress can leak financial data, while LlamaFactory’s no-network, no-files posture limits direct interaction but not downstream misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. dexter has broad network egress and scratchpad files, but LlamaFactory has no clipboard, filesystem read/write, MCP, or stdin/stdout surfaces, so a direct injection path between the pair is not evidenced.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies dexter output into LlamaFactory prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF LlamaFactory is wrapped with a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Disable any wrapper that forwards dexter text into LlamaFactory prompts.
Add provenance tags before any manual copy-paste.
requires-engineering: enforce channel separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API calls, so sensitive context can leave the local environment. LlamaFactory has no network egress or file access, so it is not the leak source, but the pair still creates a one-way exposure risk through dexter’s outbound calls.
conditions: IF dexter processes confidential financial inputs, those inputs can be sent to external APIs.
IF an operator routes the same data into dexter and then into LlamaFactory outputs, the exposure widens.
mitigations: Remove sensitive inputs from dexter runs.
Restrict dexter API keys to non-sensitive test data.
Review outbound API destinations before execution.
Log and redact prompts and tool outputs.
requires-engineering: add egress allowlists and DLP checks.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write or mutable-resource capabilities are documented. dexter can use files and network APIs, while LlamaFactory explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, so there is no plausible write-write conflict in the pair.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory is reconfigured to gain filesystem or git write access, conflict risk changes.
IF dexter is deployed with shared mutable storage not shown in the profile, new contention could appear.
mitigations: Keep LlamaFactory read-only as profiled.
Avoid shared writable directories.
Run dexter in a separate workspace.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: No evidence shows LlamaFactory automatically consumes dexter outputs as authoritative. dexter can generate research outputs and call external APIs, but LlamaFactory has no action-taking or network surfaces, so any cascade would require an external wrapper or manual handoff.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds dexter outputs directly into LlamaFactory prompts, cascade risk increases.
IF LlamaFactory is later given action tools, downstream impact becomes larger.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require source citations on dexter outputs.
Do not auto-execute LlamaFactory responses.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: dexter touches financial data and requests multiple third-party API keys, creating a compliance surface for retention and residency. LlamaFactory has no declared data classes or outbound APIs, so it is not the primary compliance driver; the risk is mainly dexter’s external processing of regulated or sensitive financial data.
conditions: IF regulated financial or market data is processed through dexter, third-party retention terms apply.
IF the operator requires strict residency or deletion guarantees, external API use may violate policy.
mitigations: Confirm data-handling terms for each dexter API.
Exclude regulated datasets from dexter runs.
Minimize retained logs and prompts.
Document deletion/export procedures.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
